provenance.notes: Pilot file. Price ranges are planning figures for a mid-size US market, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Walk gates, double drive gates, swing versus slide, automatic openers, keypad and remote access, and what a gate needs from the posts that hold it
pageStructurePlus.why: Gates are decided separately from the fence run, usually after the fence style is settled, and they carry the most hardware and the most callbacks.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Height limits, setbacks, which side faces the neighbour, the HOA approval packet, the utility locate before digging, and who files the permit
pageStructurePlus.why: Many fence jobs stall waiting on an HOA board or a permit. A page that explains the paperwork removes the reason to wait.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Survey pins, building just inside the line, sharing the cost of a boundary fence, and talking to the neighbour before the post holes go in
pageStructurePlus.why: A neighbour dispute is the fear that quietly delays the decision. Answering it in plain words gets the estimate booked.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Dog containment with dig guards and picket spacing, pool barriers with self-closing self-latching gates, privacy height, and decorative front-yard fencing
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners start from the problem, a dog that gets out or a new pool, not from a material. This page meets them there.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Leaning posts, rotted posts, broken pickets, sagging gates, wind-damaged panels, and what to document for an insurance claim
pageStructurePlus.why: Repair calls are small, fast and urgent, and a repair on an old fence is how most replacement conversations start.

designDirections.name: Yard Sign
designDirections.bestFor: Single-crew outfits that win on a fast estimate and a phone that gets answered
designDirections.whyItFits: Denim and butter reads like a work truck, and the geometric caps hold up on a phone in bright sun. The page is built around the estimate button and nothing else.

designDirections.name: Finished Lines
designDirections.bestFor: Crews with a deep backlog of finished cedar, iron and gate work to show
designDirections.headlineSample: Cedar, iron and gates, built straight in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo. The slab headings feel like a carpenter's stamp, and the linen ground lets wood grain and black iron carry the page.

designDirections.name: Estate Gate
designDirections.bestFor: Ornamental iron, custom driveway gates and estate perimeters with a long sales cycle
designDirections.headlineSample: Custom iron fences and driveway gates for {City} homes
designDirections.whyItFits: Navy and brass match powder-coated iron and gate hardware, and the serif display signals a made-to-order build rather than a quick quote.

openers.line: Your Google listing has Call and Directions but no website, so anyone comparing fence companies in {City} can't see a single gate or panel you've built before they pick up the phone.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what would sit behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing goes to your Facebook page. Fine for regulars, but someone pricing a cedar privacy fence wants styles and an estimate form, not a feed.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest fence job they shared there.
openers.linkLine: A page built for the fence buyer instead of the feed: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing still carries a free-host banner and hasn't changed in a while. Someone about to spend real money on a fence wonders if you'll be around for the gate adjustment.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a builder banner, an old copyright year or a contact form that errors. Note which one you found.
openers.linkLine: Same fence company, current and fast: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your site on my phone and the fence gallery ran off the side of the screen. People pricing a fence are often standing in their own yard, phone in hand.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note exactly what breaks: menu, gallery or call button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same fence company, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Right now the only way to ask you for a fence estimate is to call. A lot of homeowners pace off the yard after dinner and would rather send the footage and the gate count than leave a voicemail.
openers.hook: Check the listing, the social pages and any site for a form. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Here's an estimate form that asks for footage, gates and HOA status: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your cedar and iron jobs on Instagram are clean work, and they're scattered between holiday posts. A gallery sorted by fence style would do the selling for you.
openers.hook: Pick two finished jobs on their grid you could name by material and style. Mention one by name if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your fence jobs, sorted by style: {demo-link}

openers.line: You've got Google reviews about gates that finally latch and crews that cleaned up the post-hole dirt. None of that reaches anyone who isn't already on your listing.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one specific phrase about a fence or gate job. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the fence work they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Spring is when every fence company in {City} gets buried in estimate calls. The ones homeowners can find in the winter are the ones with a full spring schedule.
openers.hook: Use this from January to early March. Name the month in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready before the spring fence rush: {demo-link}

openers.line: When the neighbour's dog gets through a broken fence at nine at night, that homeowner wants a repair booked right then. Voicemail sends them to the next fence company on the list.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. If it goes to a full or generic voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A fence repair request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring fence installers. Good post-hole crews check whether a company looks established before they apply, the same way customers do.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring story, a help-wanted note or a sign on the truck. Note the date of the post.
openers.linkLine: A fence company page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing says you fence {City} and the towns around it, but there's no page telling a homeowner in {Neighborhood} you'll build there. That town name is what they type.
openers.hook: Find the towns they mention in posts or reviews. Use the one furthest from their address.
openers.linkLine: A fence page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer payment plans on fence jobs, that belongs on a page. A full backyard privacy fence is the kind of number people want split up before they ask for an estimate.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing somewhere: a post, a review, the truck. If they don't, skip this angle.
openers.linkLine: Fence financing explained before the estimate: {demo-link}

openers.line: Fence work means digging near buried lines and building on property lines. A page that shows your licence and insurance answers the first worry a careful homeowner has.
openers.hook: Check the state registry if fencing is licensed there. Note that a record exists; never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and the locate call, all in one fence page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like most of your fence work comes from neighbours seeing a finished job. That works until the street runs out, and even a referral looks you up before calling.
openers.hook: Look for review text like 'saw their fence next door' or 'neighbour recommended'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a neighbour's fence referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is clean fence work. A job like that should be the first thing a stranger sees, not three scrolls down a feed.
openers.hook: Pick the newest finished fence or gate on their grid and name it exactly: material, style, and the street if they tagged it.
openers.linkLine: That fence job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is clean fence work.

I searched for fence companies in {City} and found your social pages but no site for {Business Name}. I put together a sample page to see how your fences and gates would look with an estimate form on it, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last message got buried. Here's the sample fence site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a gallery sorted by style, an estimate form that asks for footage and gates, and a page for HOA questions. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for fence companies here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss. Short version: I built a sample fence site for {Business Name}, with an estimate form that asks for footage and gate count, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link so you can look tonight?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many style and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a fence company your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}, which is less than one backyard run."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, Tuesday or Thursday?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and an invoice for the deposit. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: I get all my work from referrals.
objections.handler: "That means your fences sell themselves. A referral still looks you up before calling, and right now they find a Facebook page. The site is where a neighbour's recommendation lands."
"Good, that's cheaper than me. Happy to hand over what I built, the style gallery and the estimate form. If it stalls before spring, the offer stands."
"That's why now is the month. The site gets built and found while it's quiet, so it's working when the spring estimate calls start."

objections.objection: I already pay for leads from a lead site.
objections.handler: "Shared leads go to several fence companies at once and you pay whether you win the job or not. Your own site sends that homeowner to one fence company."

objections.objection: People just want the cheapest fence.
objections.handler: "Some do. The site is for the ones comparing workmanship: post depth, concrete, a gate that doesn't sag. That's what makes your number make sense."
"{Build Range}. For you it'd be about {Build Price}, because it's a gallery, an estimate form and a few town pages. That's less than one fence job."

email.subject: Fence site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for fence companies in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll email you the link. Have a look when you're off the job. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} fence demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner} — spring fence season is a few weeks out and the estimate calls are about to start. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Price the gallery by project count, not page count. A fence site sells on finished jobs sorted by style.
Each material or style page is its own line once the core build is done; cedar, vinyl, iron and chain-link each answer a different search.
An estimate form that collects footage, gate count and HOA status is worth more than a contact form. Price it as its own line.
Only quote gate-automation content for companies that install openers. Otherwise leave it out of scope.
Peg the build to one mid-size privacy fence job, never to an hourly rate.
Keep storm-repair pages small and quick to build so they are ready before the next windstorm.

lineItems.description: Max when the page needs a comparison table, care notes and its own gallery of finished fences.

lineItems.item: Estimate form with footage and gate fields
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload, HOA status, a yard sketch field and routing to two estimators.
Max when it covers several towns' height and setback rules and includes a printable HOA approval checklist.
Max when it covers swing, slide and automatic gates with access-control options and opener service.
Max when each town page gets its own finished fence jobs and local permit notes.
Max with an urgent repair form, a claim-photo checklist and a banner they can switch on after a storm.
Max when the gallery captions, estimate form and HOA page are all translated, not only the home page.

whatElseYouSell.name: Finished-fence photo and drone day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One morning at your three best fence jobs, ground and drone, gives you a year of posts and a gallery that sells the next gate."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or the week they finish a job they're proud of.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile management for fence jobs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every week a new fence or gate goes on your Google profile with the town in the caption, so the map listing always has something fresh to show."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live and there's a new job to post.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests with a yard-sign code
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every finished fence gets a text asking for a review, and the yard sign carries a code the neighbours can scan."

whatElseYouSell.name: Yard sign, truck and estimate-sheet artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A new fence is a billboard for a couple of weeks. A yard sign with your name and the site on it makes it do the work."

whatElseYouSell.name: Late-winter privacy and pet fence push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A February push for privacy and dog fences lands before every other fence company's spring schedule fills."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in December, run in February.

whatElseYouSell.name: Neighbour postcards after each install
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When a fence goes up, the houses on either side get a postcard with the finished job on it. They've already seen the crew."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once there are finished jobs on the site to point at.

whatElseYouSell.name: Style sheet for realtors and HOA boards
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page fence style sheet for realtors and HOA boards puts your name in front of the people who approve and recommend fences."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, after the HOA page is live.

withoutAI.route: Landscapers and hardscapers on the same backyard jobs
withoutAI.whoPays: The landscaper, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who puts in the sod and pavers after your fence goes up? I'll build their site too, and your fence page links to theirs."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Backyard projects run in sequence and the trades already refer each other. One introduction from a fence owner is a warm door.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your fence supply yard sells to installers all over the region and their site is dated. Introduce me and I'll build their installer finder."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply yards have real budgets and their installer list is exactly the prospect list you have been building by hand.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The HOA board approves fence requests through email chains. I can build them a request page with the height and style rules on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Fence owners deal with HOA managers every week. The manager has a real problem and a budget line for resident tools.

withoutAI.route: Pool builders who need code barriers
withoutAI.whoPays: The pool builder, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every pool you fence needs a barrier that passes inspection, so the pool builders around {City} already know you. I build for them too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Pool builders sell bigger tickets than fence companies and buy websites on the same logic.

withoutAI.route: Realtors listing homes with new fences
withoutAI.pitchLine: "A new privacy fence shows up in every listing photo. The agents who sell those houses need a vendor page, and your fence company is on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents recommend vendors for a living and pay for pages that make them look organised to sellers.

withoutAI.whoPays: The trainer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Dog trainers tell owners to fix the fence before anything else. They need a site, and their clients need a fence company's number."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: A two-way referral: the trainer sends containment jobs, the fence company sends new dog owners.

withAI.route: Materials-list assistant for the supply yard's installers
withAI.pitchLine: "Give every installer on your books a tool that turns a yard sketch into a fence materials list, priced from your yard."
withAI.whyItWorks: It ties installers to one yard's prices, which is worth more to the yard than a rebate.

withAI.pitchLine: "An assistant checks each fence request against the HOA's height and style rules before the board ever sees it."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boards meet rarely and resubmissions waste everyone's month. The manager pays to stop the back-and-forth.

withAI.pitchLine: "The landscaper who shares your backyard fence jobs loses quotes to slow follow-up. Same text-back you have, built for them."
withAI.whyItWorks: You already built it once. The second build is configuration, and the referral came from a client who trusts you.

withAI.route: Pool barrier code chatbot for pool builders
withAI.pitchLine: "Pool buyers ask about barrier heights and gate latches at night. A chatbot trained on the local pool fence code answers them."
withAI.whyItWorks: Code questions slow pool sales. The fence owner's code knowledge is the training material.

withAI.pitchLine: "Property managers get broken fence and gate tickets every week. An assistant sorts them by urgency from the tenant's description and sends repairs to one fence company."
withAI.whyItWorks: The manager saves dispatch time and the fence client gets steady repair work. Both sides pay attention to it.

withAI.pitchLine: "The dealer who sells your gate openers gets the same troubleshooting calls every week. An assistant trained on their manuals takes them."
withAI.whyItWorks: Dealers carry the support cost of every installer they sell to. Cutting repeat calls is an easy budget conversation.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for fence estimate calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every missed call from the job site gets a text asking for the address and the fence they want. You call back with the answer already in hand."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their business number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Fence price calculator by style and linear foot
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner picks cedar or vinyl, enters the footage and the gates, and sees a ballpark range before they call. You stop driving out to people who wanted a cheaper fence."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their real price per foot by style, gate prices and the minimum job they take.

softwareAI.name: Photo-to-footage fence estimator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner uploads yard photos and a rough sketch, and the tool drafts the fence footage and gate count for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the calculator. Needs a set of past jobs with measured footage to tune against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job pipeline from estimate to install
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every fence estimate, deposit, locate ticket and install date on one board instead of a notebook in the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once the form is producing. Needs their stages, who estimates, and how deposits are taken.

softwareAI.name: Utility locate and permit reminder flow
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a fence job is booked, the locate request and the permit check get a reminder on the right day, so nobody digs before the lines are marked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their booking flow and which towns require a fence permit.

softwareAI.name: HOA approval packet generator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pick the fence style and the run, and it prints the HOA packet: drawing, height, materials and the spec sheet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, or the first time a job stalls on HOA approval. Needs their style specs and two past approved packets.

softwareAI.name: After-hours receptionist for fence and gate calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers at nine at night, asks for the address, the fence style and whether it's a repair, and books the estimate. You hear the recording in the morning."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once they trust you. Needs their calendar, service list and the questions they always ask. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Crew app with post-depth and photo checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The crew checks off post depth, concrete and gate swing on the phone, with a photo at each step. You see every fence job without driving to it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, when they run two crews. Needs their install checklist and a foreman willing to test it.

softwareAI.name: Materials takeoff from a site sketch
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Draw the fence line on the estimate and it lists posts, rails, pickets, concrete and gate hardware for the supply order."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their framing rules by style and a few past materials lists to check against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and progress invoicing for fence jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit at booking, balance when the last gate is hung, sent automatically with a card link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and the payment account they already use.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with style approval and install date
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner signs off on the fence style, sees the locate status and the install date, and stops calling to ask."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the job pipeline in place first.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for fence and gate jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every new review gets a reply drafted in your voice that names the fence job, ready for you to approve from your phone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside the review requests. Needs ten of their past replies to learn the voice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Gate service plan tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every automatic gate you install goes on a yearly service plan, and the tracker books the visit and bills it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, only for companies installing gate openers. Needs their opener list and a service price.

softwareAI.name: Content writer for style and town pages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new fence style or town page every month, drafted from your finished jobs and your notes, checked by you before it goes live."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their job notes and approval on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Stain and warranty check-in sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A year after a cedar fence goes in, the homeowner gets a reminder to stain it and a warranty check. That's repeat fence work from people who already said yes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a list of past jobs with install dates and the stain service price.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by fence material and crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which fence styles actually make money once materials, labour and gate hardware are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs materials invoices and crew hours for a season of jobs.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on fence styles, HOA rules and lead times
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'can I do a six-foot fence in my HOA' and 'how soon can you start' at midnight, from your real rules and schedule."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their style list, HOA notes and current lead time, updated monthly. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-estimate notes for the truck
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the fence line, talk into the phone, and it drafts the estimate with footage, gates and removal of the old fence."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their estimate template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Supplier price-sheet updater
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the supply yard changes picket and post prices, the fence calculator and the estimate template update the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after the calculator. Needs the supply yard's price sheet format.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for fence installers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for fence installer and helper jobs answer the questions you always ask, and you only call the ones with a licence and a ride."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves and the pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the fence calculator for every installer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built this fence price calculator for one company. Every fence installer in the state has the same estimate problem."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The hardest part of vertical software is knowing the workflow. The first client taught it to you and paid for the build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: License the installer finder to a fence materials distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Put a find-an-installer map on your site for every fence company that buys from you. They stay loyal to the yard that sends them work."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors spend on dealer loyalty already. A tool their installers use daily is stickier than a rebate.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Certified-installer portal for a fence manufacturer
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The vinyl or ornamental iron manufacturer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your certified fence installers need warranty registration, spec sheets and a locator. I've built that workflow for an installer already."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers have marketing budgets and a channel problem. The installer client is your proof that you know the trade.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member fence company a site template, an estimate form and an HOA page as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need reasons to renew. One deal reaches dozens of owners who already trust the association.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label fence site template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency gets fence clients and builds them from scratch. License my fence template with the estimate form and style pages built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the part you've already perfected.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Dealer locator and service requests for a gate operator distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners with a stuck gate opener search for service. A locator that routes them to your dealers keeps the work in your network."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Service requests are revenue the distributor currently loses to whoever answers first.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each of your fence territories needs town pages and an estimate form that routes to the right owner. I build it once and roll it out."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many locations, all on the same template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Fence request portal across a property management portfolio
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every community you manage gets the same fence request and approval page, with each HOA's own height and style rules."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Firms managing many associations buy once and roll out everywhere, and fence requests are a steady complaint.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: New-home fence option pages for home builders
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New-home buyers ask about a fence before closing. A fence options page in your design centre sells the upgrade and routes it to one installer."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders like upgrade revenue and a vendor who shows up organised. The fence client becomes the default installer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Monthly fence material cost sheet for installers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly sheet on where cedar, vinyl and post prices are heading, built from supply yard price lists installers share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Installers re-price jobs constantly. Built only from data they contribute, it never claims more than the sheets show.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same fence stack in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New fence clients in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I only work with one fence company per town. Yours is taken in {City}. The next metro isn't."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template, the pitch and the finished-job proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone started your fence site and disappeared. I can finish it on a template I've already shipped for another fence company."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded clients already decided to buy. They need someone who can show finished fence work fast.

upsellLadder.offer: Fence site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The fence site and the care plan go on the same contract, so a phone number change is a text to me, not a weekend for you."

upsellLadder.offer: Review requests and Google profile management
upsellLadder.trigger: The first fence job finished since launch, with photos to post.
upsellLadder.line: "That new gate job is the first thing on your Google profile now. Let's make every finished fence do that."

upsellLadder.trigger: They post a job they're proud of, or the gallery still has only a handful of fence projects.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's shoot your three best fence jobs in one morning. The gallery and a year of posts come out of it."

upsellLadder.offer: Fence price calculator by style and linear foot
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of estimate-form data shows the same styles and footage asked for again and again.
upsellLadder.line: "Most of your fence requests are the same three styles. A calculator answers them before you drive out."

upsellLadder.offer: After-hours receptionist for fence and gate calls
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention missing calls on a job, or the missed-call log shows evening repair calls.
upsellLadder.line: "Those fence repair calls after dark are going to someone else. This answers them and books the estimate."

upsellLadder.trigger: A fence job stalls waiting on an HOA board.
upsellLadder.line: "That fence job stuck at the HOA is the reason for this. The packet goes in complete the first time."

upsellLadder.offer: Job pipeline from estimate to install
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a second crew or a backlog of several weeks.
